Percorso ciclabile Balmuccia-Alagna
r.description: Percorso ciclopedonale che attraversa in lunghezza l’Alta Valsesia, con passaggio nei siti artistici e culturali più rilevanti del territorio.

r.name: B41 - Isella - Alpe Schiena
r.description: From Isella of Magugnaga to Alpe Schiena passing through Alpe Bletza. A climb in the forest initially mixed and then only of conifers, first with little slope, then alternating long steeper sections.
From the Alpe Fillar to the Bivacco Belloni. The final 50 m under the bivouac are very steep and must be traveled with particular attention.

r.name: B98a - Alpe Schena - Colle della Bottiggia
r.description: A little-used path with barely visible trail, but the presence of numerous painted signs helps. The final section is very steep, first through a jumble of enormous boulders and then over dirt and gravel.

r.name: B98 - Fornarelli, bivio B00 - Colle del Turlo
r.description: The route initially follows a path and a dirt track; from Alpe La Piana to Turlo, it follows a paved mule track built by the Alpini of the Intra Battalion in the late 1920s. The Lanti Bivouac is excellent

An interesting route featuring Walser dwellings. After a short stretch on a path, the trail ascends along a paved road and then a track, a long stone steps leads to a series of gentle terraces with views of the pass.

r.name: B33 - Parte verso Macugnaga del Sentiero Genoni
r.description: Route reserved for expert hikers with often uneven and disused tracks. Final section with small climbing sections made easier by the presence of well-maintained safety ropes.

r.name: B37 - Pra' di Lanti bivio B98 - Alpe La Pissa
B39 - Crocette - Colletto del Pizzo Nero
B47 - Sentiero Saglio
r.description: From the Zamboni Zappa Refuge to Piani Alti near the remains of the cable car. It is also known as the Silvio Saglio Trail. Its route offers a veritable balcony overlooking the wide Alpe Pedriola basin, Macugnaga, and the Anzasca Valley.

r.name: B38 - Bivio B45 - Capanna Eugenio Sella
r.description: A challenging and panoramic route on the east face of Monte Rosa that leads to the former refuge, now the Bivacco Sella, and to the crossroads for the Iacchini Pass or the Bocchetta Stenigalchi.

The route is entirely on a mule track built by the Ivrea Battalion, the other side towards Macugnaga by the Intra Battalion, the bottom is all paved with stone and as is normal on military mule tracks there are no steps.
